A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOPPLER research. All 32 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v2, including appendices, were readable and visually inspectable. Renumbered and relocated material could be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original device-assignment experiments, measured GPU execution times, training ablations, profiling, and transfer experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds GDP comparisons, policy-cost measurements, and cross-hardware transfer results.

M1.justification: The dual policies, three training stages, rewards, features, and once-per-episode message passing remain. However, v1 Section 5.2 explicitly places a LeakyReLU between two FFNN mappings in the SEL scoring network, whereas v2 Equation 4 writes only softmax(FFNN(hv)). The PDFs do not establish whether this is shorthand or an architecture revision.

E1.justification: The four workload families remain unchanged. v2 adds a distinct transfer scenario: policies trained on four P100 GPUs are evaluated on eight V100 GPUs with different connectivity, using CHAINMM and FFNN. Restricted-memory and eight-V100 evaluations already existed in v1; varying graph size alone does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GDP to the four-GPU comparison in Table 2 alongside Critical Path, Placeto, and EnumerativeOptimizer. It removes Table 2's single-GPU comparator, although single-GPU comparisons remain in Tables 8 and 9. The new timing comparison in Figure 6 evaluates DOPPLER against Placeto and GDP.

E3.justification: v2 introduces zero-shot and 2,000-episode cross-hardware transfer protocols and separately measures inference and policy-update time across graph sizes in Figure 6. GDP receives specified learning-rate and exploration schedules. Existing workload configurations and the main 4,000/8,000-episode training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds policy-cost scaling analysis and an analysis of communication locality during hardware transfer. Appendix A.3 replaces v1's completed Llama-block assignment discussion with five intermediate assignments examining node-selection order. The simulator, seed, message-passing, and Placeto-pretraining ablations are retained from v1 Appendix H as v2 Appendix G.

E5.justification: Both versions report execution-time means and standard deviations over ten executions and the same five-seed CHAINMM study. The simulator correlations are also retained. Additional result entries do not establish increased repetitions, new uncertainty procedures, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing DOPPLER runtime entries remain unchanged, but v2 adds GDP results, scaling curves, and hardware-transfer results in Tables 10–11, including 2K-shot times of 26.0 ms for CHAINMM and 14.4 ms for FFNN under the new protocol. Table 2's FFNN baseline reduction changes from 62.5% to 52.7% because GDP strengthens the comparator. Its retained Llama-layer reduction of 48.5% is inconsistent with the new best baseline: 231.5 versus 150.6 ms implies approximately 34.9%.

T1.justification: The regret objective, episodic MDP, reward definition, and training objectives are retained, without new theorems or proofs. However, the condensed SEL scoring definition in v2 Equation 4 is not demonstrably equivalent to v1's explicit nonlinear mapping. Whether that mathematical definition was substantively revised or merely abbreviated remains unresolved.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain dual-policy assignment and three-stage training for work-conserving execution. The headline reduction against the best prior baseline changes from 62.5% to 52.7% after GDP is added. The abstract also shifts its criticism of prior work from ignoring expert heuristics toward single-policy learning and insufficient optimization during deployment.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning static graphs with asynchronous execution, GNN inductive bias, sim-to-real adaptation, and computation-bound versus network-bound selection behavior. It expands scaling and hardware-transfer interpretations and removes the earlier same-hardware-only limitation after adding transfer tests. Its new annual GPU-hour savings extrapolation is unsupported by the stated 24.2 ms saving and one million daily queries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data access link, a reproducibility statement, GDP hyperparameters, and transfer-configuration information. Conversely, it omits explicit path/device embedding-sum formulas and some detailed training-stage documentation from v1. The C++ runtime description, CUDA/cuTensor versions, and principal workload and feature specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds GDP and explicitly contrasts its single placement policy with DOPPLER. It adds supporting literature on parallel matrix multiplication, bulk synchrony, collective communication, Transformers, mixture-of-experts, and parallel training. The existing list-scheduling and reinforcement-learning positioning remains; publication-metadata updates to retained references are not new related work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and training discussion, merges the problem and execution-time sections, and reorganizes the appendices to lead with assignment analyses. It adds an appendix roadmap, reproducibility statement, and acknowledgments, removes the separate limitations/societal-impact paragraph, and extensively edits terminology, captions, and citation presentation.

P2.justification: v2 extensively reformats and redistributes figures and tables. It moves the training framework into the main text, splits and relocates the FFNN comparison, adds Figure 6 and Tables 10–11, replaces the completed Llama-block display with intermediate snapshots, and removes v1's synchronous/WC schematic. The newly labeled GDP Figure 24 reuses exactly the Critical Path image from Figure 23.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens evaluation through an additional baseline, measured policy costs, and hardware-transfer tests addressing v1's explicit same-hardware limitation. It also supplies code/data access information. These gains are qualified by reporting defects: the GDP visualization duplicates Critical Path, Table 2 retains an incorrect Llama-layer reduction against the expanded baseline set, and the new annual GPU-hour estimate does not follow from its stated assumptions.
